scope: Independent mechanism-level challenge of seven user hypotheses; dedicated primary-document review only for candidate 5.
evidence_boundary: Risk deductions below are not observed spread, frequency, realized PnL, a source-backed deployment certificate or a strategy recommendation. Other workstreams own the positive evidence.
global_rejections: Do not accept a generic bridge time/cost or perp fee as every route's observed all-in cost.
Do not assume hedges improve every losing observation while leaving winning observations unchanged; include adverse hedge PnL, funding, costs and margin paths symmetrically.
Do not convert all dollar tokens at par without matching the actual issuer, claim, route and accessible redemption rights.
Do not label an ETH-correlated receipt as naturally USD hedged.
Do not originate oracle-timing, front-running, sandwiching, exploitation or manipulation strategies.
Do not turn absent evidence into a probability of zero, a 99% drawdown certificate or proof that the entire mechanism is unprofitable.

candidates.name: Perp-hedged bridge arbitrage
candidates.classification: Possible risk transfer around an inventory/settlement loop; riskless equivalence unestablished.
candidates.persistence_challenge: A persistent gap may compensate for constrained inventory, funding, margin access or settlement risk. A short hedge does not eliminate bridge/default or representation risk.
candidates.adverse_selection: A quote observed before transit need not remain executable; filled legs may be the least favorable observations.
candidates.hedge_challenge: Match underlying and perp index, quantity, time, venue collateral and unwind; funding and margin can move adversely even when a final spot spread converges.
candidates.access_and_tail_challenge: Remote collateral is not automatically usable margin. Issuer, chain and bridge dependencies remain even with small net delta.
candidates.missing_positive_evidence: The alleged 21 trades and complete contemporaneous spot/bridge/perp/margin ledgers were not read or reconstructed by this workstream.
candidates.cheapest_later_falsifier: For one independently documented event, require a symmetric, time-aligned spot-plus-hedge cash/claim ledger with both winning and losing hedge outcomes, all fees and final inventory restoration.

candidates.name: Tokenized-stock claim / perp basis
candidates.classification: Potential claim and market-access basis, not presumed redeemable cash-and-carry.
candidates.persistence_challenge: Different legal claims, issuer exposure, redemption eligibility, dividends, corporate actions and trading calendars can sustain a gap without executable convergence.
candidates.adverse_selection: Reference equity or perp marks can be unavailable or stale relative to the token venue; displayed marks are not simultaneous executable prices.
candidates.hedge_challenge: A similar ticker does not establish identical underlying rights, payoff, share ratio, index, margin currency or settlement mechanics.
candidates.access_and_tail_challenge: Issuer/perp-venue permissions, jurisdiction and stress-period redemptions must be proven from the actual instruments' terms.
candidates.missing_positive_evidence: No candidate stock issuer terms, perp specification or live redemption right was independently read in this workstream.
candidates.cheapest_later_falsifier: Compare the two instruments' exact claims and enforceable, accessible convergence path before assigning any spread to arbitrage.

candidates.name: Stablecoin-variant rail convergence
candidates.classification: Potential payment/settlement service or claim-access premium; par convergence unestablished.
candidates.persistence_challenge: Mint restrictions, inventory scarcity, finite route capacity, compliance requirements or an approaching sunset may explain the gap.
candidates.adverse_selection: An apparently cheap variant can be the one whose exit is about to tighten; a displayed redeemable price is not an available redemption allocation.
candidates.hedge_challenge: A common dollar label does not hedge a bridge haircut, issuer default or holder-specific redemption restriction.
candidates.access_and_tail_challenge: The same issuer across chains is still a common dependency. Noble's announced phases distinguish minting, ordinary redemptions, future burn-limit reductions and later conditional manual redemption.
candidates.missing_positive_evidence: No actual variant discount, executable conversion quote, current route limit or tested account entitlement was obtained.
candidates.cheapest_later_falsifier: Write the complete claim/permission/limit/date map and reject any proposed cycle requiring an unavailable mint or redemption route.

candidates.name: Public postdeployment price correction
candidates.classification: A possible lawful public-price correction hypothesis; recurring entrant edge unestablished.
candidates.persistence_challenge: Public, easy-to-replicate discrepancies invite competition. New deployment alone does not identify a repeatable payer or distinguish a genuine asset from an uneconomic representation.
candidates.adverse_selection: An observed public quote may be shallow, nonexecutable or corrected before a permitted transaction is included.
candidates.hedge_challenge: Token identity, actual transferability, depth and permitted exit venue matter more than a displayed initial price. An unmatched leg is directional inventory.
candidates.access_and_tail_challenge: New code, issuance/admin rights and venue restrictions need their own evidence; a public deployment is not a safety audit.
candidates.missing_positive_evidence: No deployed candidate token, correction event or actor profit was originated or measured.
candidates.cheapest_later_falsifier: Require one completed, public and protocol-permitted correction with real executable depth and closed inventory; exclude pending-user front-running and deployment sniping.
candidates.qualification: UNVERIFIED; NO FRONT-RUNNING OR USER SNIPING

candidates.name: Ordinary protocol-permitted liquidation and collateral risk
candidates.classification: Conditional protocol service or collateral-purchase discount; no cross-chain oracle-exploitation premise accepted.
observed_document_rules: Aave documentation makes eligibility depend on protocol Health Factor using collateral, debt and protocol-oracle values.
Aave describes a liquidator repaying debt and receiving collateral plus a reserve-specific incentive; limits depend on configuration and position conditions.
Aave aToken redemption is subject to available unborrowed liquidity and relevant collateralization constraints.
Compound III absorption assigns debt and collateral to protocol reserves; the caller receives recorded points with only possible future governance compensation.
Compound III collateral purchases are distinct from absorption and depend on reserves, inventory and protocol price feeds.
candidates.cross_chain_information_challenge: External information can inform fair-value and hedge-risk assessment; it does not itself establish the local protocol's liquidation eligibility or permission to bypass price/threshold rules.
candidates.persistence_challenge: An incentive compensates for providing debt capital, execution and collateral risk, while competition can transfer much of the value away. Compound absorber points are not a promised immediately spendable bonus.
candidates.adverse_selection: Liquidations occur under stressed collateral and liquidity conditions; apparent protocol discounts need not equal realizable sale margins.
candidates.hedge_challenge: Identify the actual collateral claim and permitted withdrawal path. A short underlying hedge cannot redeem an illiquid receipt or eliminate basis, funding, margin or settlement constraints.
candidates.access_and_tail_challenge: No target market parameters, current deployment, eligible event set or instrument-specific collateral-sale/hedge cost path was verified.
candidates.safety_rejection: Reject any variant requiring vulnerable or stale-oracle targets, manipulation or front-running of updates, timing attacks, user harm or exploit reproduction. No account targeting or execution bot was produced.
candidates.missing_positive_evidence: No eligible historical liquidation dataset, actual collateral exit quotes, hedge fill ledger or all-in cost evidence; therefore no honest candidate-specific replay or return can be supplied.
candidates.cheapest_later_falsifier: First identify the rewarded economic role, protocol eligibility and an accessible collateral-to-repayment exit. Reject any ledger that books unpromised absorption rewards or an unavailable exit.

candidates.name: Inventory-aware intent filling
candidates.classification: Potential user-funded execution/rebalancing service; inventory allocation is not itself free arbitrage.
candidates.persistence_challenge: The user may pay for timely destination inventory, but competitive auctions, solver inventory and route costs determine who retains the service margin.
candidates.adverse_selection: Firm quotes can attract fills just when prices or the cost of rebalancing move against the solver.
candidates.hedge_challenge: Completion must restore the intended inventory and settle obligations; net spot delta alone does not measure a solver's whole claim and funding book.
candidates.access_and_tail_challenge: Prove actual solver eligibility, permitted orderflow access, settlement verification, any bonds or locked funds, and fallback behavior. These details are protocol-specific, not assumed present in every design.
candidates.missing_positive_evidence: This workstream did not read a specific intent auction, solver bond specification or completed paid fill.
candidates.cheapest_later_falsifier: For an already documented completed fill, distinguish user service payment from inventory mark changes and include the full time and cost until capital is reusable.

candidates.name: LST/LRT discount and redemption
candidates.classification: Potential redemption/issuer/protocol liquidity basis, not naturally USD-neutral.
candidates.persistence_challenge: Queue duration, withdrawal permissions, staking/restaking losses and claim uncertainty may justify a discount. Expected yield is not a guaranteed redemption date or amount.
candidates.adverse_selection: Discounts can deepen when redemption queues, volatility and exit demand rise together.
candidates.hedge_challenge: An ETH-linked asset remains exposed to ETH/USD unless separately hedged; a perp hedge still leaves claim-conversion, funding and margin risks.
candidates.access_and_tail_challenge: Underlying validator, restaking, issuer, protocol and chain dependencies may overlap across superficially different receipts.
candidates.missing_positive_evidence: No particular LST/LRT redemption terms, queue measurements or realized conversion history was read here; the audit/settlement workstreams own instrument-specific evidence.
candidates.cheapest_later_falsifier: Match the exact receipt to an accessible redemption claim and separately account for USD exposure, variable redemption time and adverse hedge funding.

recommendation: Keep the hypothesis map open where evidence is missing, but reject claimed near-risklessness and unsafe oracle/user-harm variants. No allocation or next research wave authorized by this critique.
